html:
In August 1185 the Normans of the Kingdom of Sicily stormed and sacked Thessalonica, the second city of the Byzantine Empire. It was one of the worst disasters to strike the empire in the 12th century.

King William II of Sicily used the chaos of Andronikos I's reign as a chance to invade. His army took Dyrrhachium and marched across the Balkans while his fleet sailed round Greece. The governor, David Komnenos, made a poor defence, and after a short siege the Normans broke in. Thousands of citizens were killed and churches were looted. The archbishop, the scholar Eustathios, survived and wrote an eyewitness account.

The news caused panic in Constantinople and brought down Andronikos, who was killed by a mob. The new emperor, Isaac II Angelos, sent the general Alexios Branas, who beat the Normans at Dimitritzes later that year and drove them out.
